items.sentence: Its brass tubing coils into a compact shape before widening into a flared bell.
A small cup-shaped mouthpiece sits at one end, while rotary valves are fitted along the tubing.
Many orchestral models have three main valves, each connected to an additional length of tubing.
Double models add a thumb-operated change valve that lets players switch between F and B-flat tubing.
Players buzz their lips against the mouthpiece while exhaling to set the air column vibrating.
Pressing a valve redirects airflow through extra tubing, lowering the pitch produced by the instrument.
A player's right hand inside the bell can alter the instrument's intonation and tone color.
Players adjust lip tension and airflow to produce notes across the instrument's broad range.
In symphony orchestras, these instruments typically sit in the brass section behind the strings and woodwinds.
Wind ensembles often include several players on this instrument, grouped together within the brass section.
During some quiet passages, a player may insert a mute into the bell to change the sound.
In chamber music, a single player may join woodwind performers in a small mixed ensemble.
Its rounded, sustained tones help fill out the harmony in orchestral music.
Composers often assign it lyrical melodies that can stand out above the ensemble.
Its ability to blend with strings and woodwinds makes it useful for connecting contrasting sections of an ensemble.
In film scores, its wide range and rich tone can contribute to dramatic musical passages.
